Artemis II was a crewed lunar flyby mission that took place from April 1 to April 11, 2026.
Artemis II's crew comprised four astronauts: Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen.
Artemis II's spacecraft, named Integrity, was manufactured by Lockheed Martin for the Orion module and Airbus for the European Service Module.
Artemis II launched from Kennedy Space Center's Launch Complex 39B aboard a Space Launch System rocket on April 1, 2026.
Artemis II's closest approach to the Moon occurred on April 6, 2026, at a distance of 4,067 miles.
Artemis II set a new record for the greatest human distance from Earth, reaching 252,756 miles during its flyby.
Artemis II's mission duration was exactly 9 days, 1 hour, 32 minutes, and 15 seconds.
Artemis II's crew broke the record for the most people in deep space at once, surpassing the Apollo 8 count of three.
Artemis II's reentry trajectory was modified to a steeper direct entry to mitigate risks from heat shield erosion observed after Artemis I.
Artemis II was recovered by the USS John P. Murtha in the Pacific Ocean southwest of San Diego on April 11, 2026.
Artemis II carried the zero-gravity indicator plush toy named Rise, which was designed by eight-year-old Lucas Ye.
Artemis II's optical communications system, O2O, achieved a downlink rate of up to 260 megabits per second.
Artemis II's crew included Jeremy Hansen, the first non-American astronaut to travel around the Moon.
Artemis II's wake-up calls included a posthumous message from Apollo astronaut Jim Lovell recorded in August 2025.
Artemis II's mission objectives were similar to those of Apollo 8, though it did not enter lunar orbit due to propulsion limitations.
